key_insight: CCL reduces teacher bias in LLM distillation by alternately calibrating the teacher on source rewards and updating the student on target questions, yielding convergence toward the oracle student without target-domain reward feedback.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical distillation strategy for domain-shifted LLM deployment when target labels or rewards are unavailable, helping smaller models inherit useful behavior while limiting systematic teacher errors.
method: Calibrate the teacher using source-domain reward feedback only.
Use token-level branching to generate calibrated target-question supervision for the student.
Iterate student updates and teacher recalibration in a coupled loop under an autoregressive policy framework.
evidence_signal: The theory shows the student’s expected average KL divergence to the oracle student converges to zero at a polynomial rate, and it proves a separation from direct matching that can stay suboptimal even when the teacher is better than all student policies.
watch_item: The guarantee is theoretical and depends on iterative calibration quality, so practical performance may be sensitive to source-target shift, branching design, and optimization stability.
paper_title: Coupled Calibration and Learning: Mitigating Teacher Bias in LLM Distillation without Target-Domain Reward Feedback
